claim: DNN training interruptions can erase work since the last persisted checkpoint; epoch-level checkpointing can lose substantial training time.
locator: Mohan et al., FAST 2021, Abstract and Sections 1–2, pp. 203–204
notes: Historical motivation from the paper; do not generalize its cluster failure rates to current LLM clusters.

claim: CheckFreq separates checkpointing into snapshot and persist phases and carefully overlaps them with computation while preserving a consistent snapshot boundary.
notes: The next parameter update must not race with an unfinished snapshot copy.

claim: CheckFreq profiles iteration, snapshot and storage costs, chooses an initial checkpoint frequency and adapts it to runtime interference.
notes: This is a framework-specific policy, not the same algorithm as the simple Young-Daly calculator in this article.

claim: In the paper's evaluated configurations, CheckFreq checkpointed 83–278 times more frequently than epoch-level policies while incurring at most 3.5% runtime overhead.
notes: Preserve the paper's hardware/model scope; this is not a current LLM training benchmark.

claim: For BERT in the paper's single-V100 configuration, average recovery time was reported as 4920 seconds for the baseline and 85 seconds for CheckFreq.
locator: Table 6, p. 211, column (a), 1 GPU (V100), BERT row
notes: Historical result under the paper's specific training and interruption setup.

claim: The first-order checkpoint interval is approximately sqrt(2*C*M), where C is checkpoint duration and M is mean time between failures.
locator: Daly (2006), Section 2; first-order approximation and discussion of Young's estimate
notes: The article derives the simplified overhead C/tau + tau/(2M). It explicitly labels the stationary Poisson and uniform failure-position assumptions.

claim: Young-Daly interval models are approximations whose applicability depends on failure assumptions and workflow structure.
locator: A survey on checkpointing strategies: Should we always checkpoint à la Young/Daly?, Future Generation Computer Systems 161 (2024)
notes: Supports the article's warning against treating the formula as a universal production policy.

claim: PyTorch Distributed Checkpoint saves and loads across multiple ranks, stores multiple files and supports load-time resharding.
notes: API behavior and compatibility are version-sensitive; consult the installed PyTorch version.

claim: DCP async_save stages state into memory buffers before background storage writes; staging and in-flight request management have additional memory and synchronization requirements.
locator: Asynchronous Checkpointing Overview and async_save examples
notes: The tutorial recommends limiting concurrent outstanding checkpoint requests for most users.

claim: PyTorch 2.9 introduced DefaultStager and async_stager to move state-dict construction and D2H staging into a background thread.
notes: Requires checking the installed PyTorch version and hardware-specific memory/CPU constraints.

claim: Megatron Core documents dp_reshardable as faster but not model-parallel reshardable, while fully_reshardable is more flexible and slower.
notes: The exact format and support depend on Megatron Core version.

claim: DeepSpeed provides ZeRO checkpoint conversion to consolidated FP32 weights and documents Universal Checkpoints as under development.
locator: ZeRO checkpoint FP32 weights recovery and Universal Checkpoints
notes: A consolidated inference/model artifact is not automatically a full training-resume checkpoint.

claim: PyTorch activation checkpointing trades compute for memory by recomputing forward intermediates during backward.
notes: Included to distinguish activation checkpointing from persistent training checkpoints.
